newsitem.title: USA: USDA corrects Kansas weekly crop progress figures.
newsitem.headline: USDA corrects Kansas weekly crop progress figures.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Tuesday that the Kansas winter wheat crop was in worse condition than it reported Monday in the weekly U.S. crop progress report.
In issuing an official correction, the USDA said that only 54 percent of the Kansas winter wheat crop was in good condition as of the week ended June 22, not 64 percent as it reported on Monday.

The USDA correction also affected the national ratings for the U.S. winter wheat crop, lowering the amount in good-to-excellent condition to 63 percent, from the 67 percent incorrectly reported on Monday.
The USDA also corrected the Kansas figures for corn and soybean crop conditions.
It said the Kansas corn crop was now rated 63 percent good and 23 percent excellent, compared to the incorrect figures of 83 percent good and one percent excellent reported on Monday.

The correction slightly affected the overall national ranking of corn crop conditions. Conditions in the principle 17 corn-growing states are now rated 54 percent good and 13 percent excellent, compared to the incorrect figures of 55 percent good and 12 percent excellent reported on Monday.
The agency said it also corrected the Kansas condition numbers for the state's soybean crop.

USDA said Kansas soybeans were now 74 percent good and 12 excellent, rather than the incorrect figures of 85 percent good and one percent excellent issued on Monday. However, the overall crop condition ratings for the 19 principle soybean-growing states were not affected by the change for Kansas.
